title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is almost entirely illegible: very faint, heavily abbreviated handwriting, struck through by three long diagonal strokes, with a short brown-ink marginal note at lower left. Only scattered symbols can be read: a heading 'La catégorie des …', a diagram 'S ←π U_0' with 'U' below (apparently 'U … lisse'), a Hom between pairs '(U_0, V_0)', '(U, V)', a product written '(U_0 ×_S V_0, U × V)', the pair '(U, U_0)', the symbols 'D_S', a script letter (E or G), 'A', a script 'D', 'U_0 … U … )!', and 'S × S' at the end.

Plausible reconstruction, not certain. Grothendieck seems to be defining a category whose objects are pairs (U, U_0), where U_0 is an S-scheme (U_0 → S) embedded as a closed subscheme of a smooth (or arbitrary) scheme U, presumably a thickening. Morphisms would be compatible pairs of maps, and products would be formed as (U_0 ×_S V_0, U × V). A 'D_S' construction and the diagonal in S × S would then enter. This is the standard set-up of the infinitesimal or crystalline site (or the category of 'embeddings') used to define the de Rham / infinitesimal cohomology of U_0/S. In this context it would serve as an intrinsic definition of the Gauss–Manin connection, through the stratification on S given by the neighbourhoods of the diagonal in S × S.

By the reading direction, the page sits between neighbouring pages on the obstruction to integrable connections on line bundles and the p-curvature/Cartier computation. It is therefore probably a discarded digression, cancelled by the strike-through, on a site-theoretic framework for Gauss–Manin.
